;Business and Economy
*[[Fiat Chrysler Automobiles|Fiat Chrysler]] CEO [[Sergio Marchionne]] resigns due to failing health and is replaced by [[Jeep]] CEO [[Michael Manley (CEO)|Mike Manley]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2018/07/21/business/fiat-chrysler-ceo.amp.html (''The New York Times'')]

;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Western Iran clashes (2016–present)]]
**[[Kurdistan Free Life Party|PJAK]] militants blow up an ammunition dump and kill eleven [[Iran]]ian [[Islamic Republic of Iran Border Guard Command|border guards]] stationed at an [[Iran–Iraq border]] post in [[Marivan County]]. Several militants are killed in return.  [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iran-security-clash/militants-kill-10-iran-guards-at-iraqi-border-post-agency-idUSKBN1KB0DV (Reuters)] 
*[[Syrian Civil War]]
**[[Israel Defense Forces]] extract 98 [[White Helmets (Syrian Civil War)|White Helmets]] and 324 others from recently recaptured southwestern [[Syria]]n territory into [[Jordan]], at the request of [[Canada]] and the [[United States]]. Canada, the [[United Kingdom]] and [[Germany]] offer refuge to some of them. Two other groups intended for rescue, comprising about 800 people, do not escape. [https://www.cbc.ca/amp/1.4749380 (CBC)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2018 Vietnam floods]]
**[[Tropical_Storm_Son-Tinh_(2018)|Tropical Storm Son-Tinh]] kills 20 people, injures 14 more and leaves at least 16 missing in [[Vietnam]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-asia-storm-vietnam/storm-son-tinh-kills-20-leaves-16-missing-in-vietnam-idUSKBN1KB0JZ (Reuters)]
*The death toll from a heatwave in [[Japan]] rises to 30. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-44910435 (BBC)]

;Law and crime
*[[Crime in South Africa]]
**Gunmen attack a minibus of people returning from a funeral between [[Colenso, KwaZulu-Natal|Colenso]] and [[Weenen]] in [[KwaZulu-Natal]], [[South Africa]]. Eleven people are shot dead and four others are critically injured. [https://www.standard.co.uk/news/crime/south-africa-shooting-11-killed-as-gunmen-open-fire-on-minibus-a3893206.html (''The Evening Standard'')]
*[[2018 Los Angeles hostage incident]]
**A gunman is arrested for one count of murder after killing a woman then taking dozens of people hostage at a [[Trader Joe's]] in [[Los Angeles]], [[California]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/trader-joes-shooting-hostage-suspect-arrested-hostages-freed-silver-lake-los-angeles-live-updates-2018-07-22/ (CBS News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[People's Party (Spain) leadership election, 2018]]
**[[Pablo Casado]] is elected leader of [[Spain]]'s centre-right [[People's Party (Spain)|People's Party]] after defeating former [[Deputy Prime Minister of Spain]] [[Soraya Sáenz de Santamaría]] in a run-off. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-44911875 (BBC)]
*[[Presidency of Rodrigo Duterte]]
**The [[Philippines]] immigration authority has ordered the deportation and blacklisting of an Australian nun who was investigated, under instruction from [[President of the Philippines|President]] [[Rodrigo Duterte]], for her political activism. [http://www.businessinsider.com/philippines-rodrigo-duterte-patricia-fox-nun-deportation-2018-7 (''Business Insider'')]

;Sports
*[[2018 Rugby World Cup Sevens – Women's tournament]]
**[[New Zealand women's national rugby sevens team|New Zealand]] defeats [[France women's national rugby sevens team|France]] 29–0 in the final to win the 2018 women's [[Rugby World Cup Sevens]]. [https://www.radionz.co.nz/news/sport/362345/black-ferns-sevens-dominate-france-for-world-cup-win (Radio New Zealand)]
